name: When should I repair a roof leak versus replacing the entire roof?

mainEntity.name: When should I repair a roof leak versus replacing the entire roof?

acceptedAnswer.text: Deciding between repair and replacement hinges on your roof's age, the extent of the damage, and its overall condition. If your roof is relatively new (under 10-15 years) and the leak is localized and minor, a repair is usually sufficient. However, if your roof is nearing the end of its expected lifespan (20+ years), has multiple leaks, widespread damage, or shows signs of significant wear, a full replacement might be a more cost-effective long-term solution. A professional assessment can determine the best course.
acceptedAnswer.description: Repair if your roof is new and the leak is minor; replace if it's old, has widespread damage, or multiple leaks.
